questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The canons are being fired continuously by them.
options: They fired canons continuously.
They are firing the canons continuously.
They have fired the canons continuously.
The canons fire continuously.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Continuous tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Continuous.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

For example:

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: They are firing the canons continuously.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Access denied.
options: Let the access be denied.
Access is being denied.
Let it be known that access will be denied.
Access has been denied.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The question in Active voice is in the imperative form. An imperative sentence is used to express order, request, suggestion, etc. They begin with a principal verb. Here, the imperative sentence in Active voice is an order.

The format in Active voice is: V1 + Object.

Thus, the format in Passive voice will be: Let + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + be + V3.

For example:

Start the match. (Active)

Let the match be started. (Passive)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): Let the access be denied.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The rescue team could have completed the task if there had been uninterrupted power supply.
options: The task could have been completed by the rescue team if there had been uninterrupted power supply.
The task could be completed by the rescue team if there was uninterrupted power supply.
The task could have to be completed by the rescue team if there was uninterrupted power supply.
The task can have completed by the rescue team if there was uninterrupted power supply.
questions.solution:
In passive voice, the object (task) becomes the subject, and "could have completed" becomes "could have been completed." Accordingly, the option that follows these rules of passive voice is "The task could have been completed by the rescue team if there had been uninterrupted power supply."

Option (b): This is present conditional, not matching the past conditional "could have."

Option (c): This is grammatically awkward and incorrect.

Option (d): This is incorrect; "can have completed" is not a valid construction.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question:

Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team.
questions.solution:
· The active voice sentence is in present continuous tense ("is conducting").

· To convert it to passive voice, we follow the structure:

Object + is/are being + past participle + by + subject

· Option 4 correctly follows this structure:

"Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team."

· Option 1 changes the tense incorrectly.

· Option 2 uses past continuous, which is incorrect.

· Option 3 has an incorrect structure and wording.

Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

I remember my mother taking me to the stadium.
options: I was taken to the stadium by mother that I remembered.
My mother remembered me taken to the stadium.
I remember being taken to the stadium by my mother.
I was remembered being taken to the stadium by my mother.
questions.solution:
To convert the active voice sentence "I remember my mother taking me to the stadium" to passive voice, we focus on the verb phrase "taking me to the stadium." In passive voice:

The object "me" becomes the subject.

The verb "taking" (present participle) changes to "being taken" (passive form).

The subject "my mother" becomes the agent, introduced by "by."

The verb "remember" remains unchanged, as it is not the verb being converted to passive. The structure becomes: "I remember being taken to the stadium by my mother."

Checking the options:

Option 1: "I was taken to the stadium by mother that I remembered" is grammatically incorrect and changes the meaning.

Option 2: "My mother remembered me taken to the stadium" incorrectly shifts the subject and is awkward.

Option 3: "I remember being taken to the stadium by my mother" is correct, maintaining the original meaning in passive voice.

Option 4: "I was remembered being taken to the stadium by my mother" incorrectly applies passive to "remember."

Thus, option 3 is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Doctors saved many lives during the pandemic.
options: Many lives have been saved by doctors during the pandemic.
Many lives were being saved by doctors during the pandemic.
Many lives were saved by doctors during the pandemic.
Many lives are saved by doctors during the pandemic.
questions.solution:
To convert the active voice sentence "Doctors saved many lives during the pandemic" to passive voice:

The object "many lives" becomes the subject.

The verb "saved" (past simple) changes to "were saved" (past simple passive, as "lives" is plural).

The subject "doctors" becomes the agent, introduced by "by."

The sentence becomes: "Many lives were saved by doctors during the pandemic."

Checking the options:

Option 1: "Many lives have been saved" uses present perfect, which does not match the past simple tense.

Option 2: "Many lives were being saved" uses past continuous, implying an ongoing action, which is less appropriate.

Option 3: "Many lives were saved" correctly uses past simple passive.

Option 4: "Many lives are saved" uses present tense, which does not match the past context.

Thus, option 3 is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The new sunshades have protected our windows during the rainy season.
options: Our windows are being protected by the new window during the rainy season.
Our windows are being protected by the new sunshades during the rainy season.
Our sunshades have been protected by the windows during the rainy season.
Our windows have been protected by the new during the rainy season.
questions.solution:
To convert the active voice sentence to passive voice:

The object ("our windows") becomes the subject.

The verb "have protected" (present perfect) becomes "have been protected" (passive form: have/has + been + past participle).

The subject ("the new sunshades") becomes the agent, introduced by the preposition "by."

The correct option that maintains the tense (present perfect) and uses "sunshades" correctly is option (4), "Our windows have been protected by the new sunshades during the rainy season."

(a) Our windows are being protected by the new window: Incorrect tense (present continuous "are being protected" vs. present perfect). Also, "window" is incorrect; the original subject is "sunshades."

(b) Our windows are being protected by the new sunshades: Incorrect tense (present continuous instead of present perfect).

(c) Our sunshades have been protected by the new windows: Correct tense but wrong subject ("windows" instead of "sunshades").

Hence, the correct answer is option (3).
